title: Do Google Local Service Ads Work for Local Service Businesses?  - Accrisoft

facts.fact: Google Local Service Ads (LSAs) are pay-per-lead ads that target users searching for local services.
facts.quote: Google Local Service Ads (LSAs) are pay-per-lead ads that target users searching for local services.

facts.fact: LSAs appear at the top of search results, before any organic or paid listings, and are marked with a green checkmark indicating that Google has vetted the business.
facts.quote: These ads appear at the top of the search results page, before any organic or paid listings, and are marked with a green checkmark indicating that Google has vetted the business.

facts.fact: To participate in LSAs, businesses must meet specific criteria, including background checks and licensing requirements.
facts.quote: To participate in the program, businesses must meet specific criteria, including background checks and licensing requirements

facts.fact: Under LSAs, businesses pay a predetermined fee for each lead generated rather than paying for clicks or impressions.
facts.quote: Rather than paying for clicks or impressions, businesses pay a predetermined fee for each lead generated through the ads.

facts.fact: LSAs are cost-per-lead, while Google Ads can be cost-per-click or cost-per-impression, according to Accrisoft.
facts.quote: LSAs are cost-per-lead, while Google Ads can be cost-per-click or cost-per-impression.

facts.fact: Accrisoft states that LSAs can be more expensive than other forms of online advertising, especially for highly competitive keywords.
facts.quote: LSAs can be more expensive than other forms of online advertising, especially for highly competitive keywords.

facts.fact: Google Ads was formerly known as Google AdWords.

Google provides a dashboard for monitoring the performance of Local Service Ads (LSAs), where advertisers can track metrics such as number of leads generated, cost per lead, and overall return on investment.
facts.quote: Yes, Google provides a dashboard where you can monitor the performance of your LSAs. You can track metrics such as the number of leads generated, the cost per lead, and the overall return on investment.
